title: Add mistake category with per-class and per-cause counts
summary: Retry of job 20261023-183334-aej6: add a `mistake` intervention category. Status, the audit and the JSON count mistakes per class and per cause, apart from interventions_by_category. Introspecting a mistake proposes the preventing check or knowledge. This time a test must read the audit output, and the audit must print mistakes even when no job audit is produced. The audience is Sri.

defaults_applied.how: Every new behavior has a named test; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check counts appearing in status and audit output, not just the new type.
A criterion requires a reader to see mistake counts, recurring causes and proposed prevention.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
The pipeline evidence gate is left out and the change stays on the mistake category.
All changes are Rust and Markdown.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The request as typed is 'try again' on the original mistakes job, so the original request is the goal. The pre-handover evidence check proposed by the introspection is a separate pipeline change and is not built here.
The producer maps every criterion to a named test before finishing; this is the lesson of the earlier rejection, kept as a working practice and not as a new mechanism.
Mistakes are interventions with category `mistake`, plus legacy interventions with category `other` whose text starts 'Mistake:'. Existing records are not rewritten.
The previous attempt's file list is the starting point. It adds crates/athena-cli/tests/auditor.rs for the missing audit test and docs/design/athena-v0.md, which lists the category set.
The audit's mistake report must not depend on a job audit being produced, so it prints before the early return in Command::Audit in main.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: new tests show an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and appears in `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and an unknown category is still rejected with an error listing `mistake`.

Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows `athena status` output and its JSON report mistake counts per class and per cause, in fields separate from `interventions_by_category`.

Run `cargo test`: a CLI test in crates/athena-cli/tests (auditor.rs or introspection.rs) runs the audit command and asserts its output reports mistakes per class and per cause. A second case asserts the mistake counts still print when no job audit is produced.

Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention yields a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it, and that mistakes with the same cause aggregate into one proposal.

Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and `cargo test` passes in full.

Outcome-check: a reader of the status or audit output can see how many mistakes occurred, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention work was proposed. README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the category list in docs/design/athena-v0.md mention the `mistake` category.

out_of_scope: Building the pre-handover evidence gate in the job pipeline, which the introspection proposed as a separate next request
Rewriting or migrating existing intervention records
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow files
departures: Cost and time are raised above the reference because the change spans about 10 files, and the previous attempt failed verification. Pass probability is slightly raised because the missing audit test is now an explicit criterion.
